name: Payhip
tagline: Sell downloads and simple courses through Stripe or PayPal

pricing.notes: Official Plus monthly tier plus reduced transaction fee.

tiers.name: Free Forever
tiers.limits: Unlimited products and revenue; 5% Payhip transaction fee.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: Unlimited products and revenue; 2% Payhip transaction fee.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited products and revenue; 0% Payhip transaction fee.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited products and revenue with a 5% Payhip transaction fee
pricing.hiddenCosts: Stripe or PayPal processing fees apply on every plan in addition to Payhip's 5%/2%/0% platform fee.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Payhip, sell downloads and simple courses through Stripe or PayPal. The hard boundary is payment integration, eu and uk vat handling, affiliates, courses, and hosted delivery, plus payments, tax, distribution, and operations.
coreLoopDIY: Sell a small catalog of downloads and simple courses through Stripe or PayPal, deliver purchased files or lessons, and manage customers from a user-owned storefront.
whatYouLose: payment integration, EU and UK VAT handling, affiliates, courses, and hosted delivery
ongoingBurden: checkout, webhooks, tax, refunds, fraud, entitlements, storage, email, accessibility, backups, and customer support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Payhip because creators pay to outsource the dangerous and tedious parts around money, delivery, tax, and customer access. The recurring cost buys checkout, webhooks, tax, refunds, fraud, entitlements, storage, email, accessibility, backups, and customer support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Medusa
priorArt.desc: Active open-source commerce platform with modular checkout and fulfillment primitives.

alternatives.name: CourseLit
alternatives.desc: Courses and downloadable products with payments and sales pages; the free route is a Docker deployment.

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: Downloads, one course, checkout and email on a permanent free plan; more products fit better than more courses.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Medusa
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A headless shop does not supply the ready-made course and download experience Payhip combines.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Moodle
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Courses are excellent; the simple digital-download storefront is missing.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Vvveb
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It sells downloads well, but it is not a lesson, quiz and progress-tracking course platform.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Plus plan and a single-creator storefront DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Payhip in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Stripe Checkout, and S3-compatible storage; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: sell a small catalog of downloads and simple courses through Stripe or PayPal, deliver purchased files or lessons, and manage customers from a user-owned storefront.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement products, variants, prices, files or lessons, coupons, customers, orders, and entitlements.
Use Stripe-hosted Checkout and verify every webhook signature and idempotency key.
Grant access only after confirmed payment and revoke it on refund or chargeback.
Create a customer library with signed short-lived download or lesson URLs.
Add order search, resend receipt, refund handoff, export, and an immutable event log.
Document taxes as the creator's responsibility and do not calculate unsupported jurisdictions.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out merchant-of-record tax remittance.
Deliberately leave out a buyer marketplace or affiliate network.
Deliberately leave out advanced communities, certificates, mobile apps, and enterprise learning features.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
